o.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish دپوك (depük). By surface analysis, təp- + -ik.
Borrowed from Classical Persian جَمَادِیُالثَّانِی (jamādiyu-s-sānī), from Arabic جُمَادَى الثَّانِي (jumādā ṯ-ṯānī), ellipsis of شَهْر جُمَادَى الثَّانِي (šahr jumādā ṯ-ṯānī).
Ultimately from French psychologie, reinterpreted as an adjective.
